tips.headline: Use @-mentions to give Claude Code precise file context
tips.summary: Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code, recommends using @-mentions to point Claude at specific files instead of letting it search. This dramatically reduces token usage and improves accuracy since Claude works with the exact files you intend rather than guessing from project structure.
actionable_steps: Type @ in Claude Code to see a file picker with fuzzy search
Select the specific files relevant to your task before writing your prompt
Combine multiple @-mentions for cross-file tasks like refactoring

tips.headline: Write a CLAUDE.md file to set project conventions once
tips.summary: Adding a CLAUDE.md to your project root lets you define coding standards, test commands, and architectural decisions that persist across every Claude Code session. Think of it as onboarding documentation that Claude reads automatically — you teach it once instead of repeating yourself.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md in your project root with build/test/lint commands
Add coding conventions like naming patterns, preferred libraries, and file structure
Include architectural decisions and constraints Claude should respect
Use /init in Claude Code to auto-generate a starter CLAUDE.md

tips.headline: Use Claude's extended thinking for complex architectural decisions
tips.summary: When asking Claude to make non-trivial design choices — like choosing between patterns, structuring a new module, or planning a migration — enabling extended thinking produces significantly better results. Claude will reason through trade-offs before committing to an approach, catching issues that quick responses miss.
actionable_steps: For architecture questions, ask Claude to 'think through the trade-offs' explicitly
Use Claude Code's plan mode (shift+tab) for multi-step tasks that need careful reasoning
Review Claude's reasoning in extended thinking to catch flawed assumptions early

sources.title: Tips for getting better architectural advice from Claude

tips.headline: Enable PowerShell tool for Windows development workflows
tips.summary: Claude Code now includes an opt-in PowerShell tool that allows Windows users to execute PowerShell commands directly through Claude. This provides native Windows command-line access for system administration and development tasks.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.84 or later
Enable the PowerShell tool in your settings as a preview feature
Visit https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#powershell-tool for configuration details

tips.headline: Configure streaming timeout for better connection handling
tips.summary: The new CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable lets you customize how long Claude Code waits before timing out idle streaming connections. This helps prevent unnecessary disconnections during long-running operations.
actionable_steps: Set the CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable
Choose a timeout value in milliseconds (default is 90000 for 90 seconds)
Restart Claude Code for the setting to take effect

tips.headline: Use managed settings drop-in directory for team policy deployment
tips.summary: The new managed-settings.d/ directory allows multiple teams to deploy independent configuration fragments that automatically merge. This enables better organization of team-specific policies without conflicts.
actionable_steps: Create a managed-settings.d/ directory alongside your managed-settings.json
Place individual team policy files in the directory (they merge alphabetically)
Name files with prefixes to control merge order (e.g., 01-team-a.json, 02-team-b.json)

tips.headline: Use environment variables to configure MCP server settings in Claude Code
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.85 introduced CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME and CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variables for MCP headersHelper scripts. This allows a single helper script to serve multiple MCP servers, simplifying configuration management.
actionable_steps: Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME environment variable to your desired server name
Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variable to your MCP server URL
Update your MCP headersHelper scripts to use these variables instead of hardcoded values

tips.headline: Add session tracking header for proxy aggregation
tips.summary: Use the `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` header in your API requests to help proxies group requests by session without needing to parse request bodies. This improves routing and monitoring capabilities when using Claude Code through proxy servers.
actionable_steps: Add the `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` header to your Claude Code API requests
Set the header value to your session identifier
Configure your proxy to use this header for request aggregation instead of body parsing

tips.headline: Set CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1 to eliminate screen flickering
tips.summary: This environment variable enables flicker-free alt-screen rendering with virtualized scrollback in Claude Code v2.1.88+. It provides a smoother visual experience when Claude Code switches between screen modes during long coding sessions.
actionable_steps: Add 'export CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1' to your shell profile (.bashrc, .zshrc, etc.)
Restart your terminal or run 'source ~/.bashrc' to apply the change
Launch Claude Code to verify flicker-free rendering is active

tips.headline: Use defer permission in PreToolUse hooks to pause headless sessions
tips.summary: You can now pause headless Claude Code sessions at tool calls and resume them later with permission evaluation. This allows for better control over automated workflows that need human approval.
actionable_steps: Set up a PreToolUse hook in your Claude Code configuration
Return 'defer' as the permission decision in the hook
Resume the session using `claude-code -p --resume` command
The hook will re-evaluate the tool call upon resumption

tips.headline: Use /powerup command to learn Claude Code features interactively
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.90 introduced the /powerup command that provides interactive lessons with animated demos to help you learn Claude Code features. This is particularly useful for new users who want to quickly understand the tool's capabilities through hands-on tutorials.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.90 or later
Type `/powerup` in the Claude Code interface
Follow the interactive lessons and animated demos to learn features

tips.headline: Use _meta annotation to prevent large MCP tool results from being truncated
tips.summary: Claude Code now supports preserving large tool results (like database schemas) up to 500K characters by adding a special metadata annotation. This prevents important data from being cut off during processing.
actionable_steps: Add `_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]` annotation to your MCP tool result
Set the value to your desired character limit (up to 500,000)
Test with large results like database schemas to verify they pass through completely

tips.headline: Use forceRemoteSettingsRefresh policy to ensure fresh configuration on startup
tips.summary: This setting forces Claude Code CLI to fetch the latest remote managed settings before starting and exits if the fetch fails. This ensures your CLI always runs with the most current configuration and prevents running with stale settings that might cause issues.
actionable_steps: Open your Claude Code CLI configuration
Add the policy setting `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true`
Restart the CLI to verify it blocks startup until fresh settings are fetched

tips.headline: Enable Amazon Bedrock support with Mantle integration
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.94 added support for Amazon Bedrock through Mantle integration. This allows you to use Claude Code with Amazon's Bedrock service instead of the default API endpoints, potentially offering better performance or compliance for enterprise users.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE=1 in your system or terminal
Restart Claude Code to apply the new configuration
Verify the connection is working by running a test query

tips.headline: Set up Google Vertex AI integration using the interactive wizard
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.98 introduced a guided setup wizard that simplifies connecting to Google Vertex AI. This eliminates manual configuration steps and reduces authentication errors by walking you through GCP setup, project selection, and credential verification.
actionable_steps: Open Claude Code and go to the login screen
Select '3rd-party platform' option
Follow the interactive Google Vertex AI setup wizard
Complete GCP authentication, project and region configuration, and credential verification as prompted

tips.headline: Use `/team-onboarding` command to generate teammate ramp-up guides
tips.summary: Claude Code can automatically create onboarding documentation for new team members based on your local usage patterns. This saves time creating training materials and ensures consistency in how team members learn your workflows.
actionable_steps: Update to Claude Code v2.1.101 or later
Run the `/team-onboarding` command in your Claude Code interface
Review the generated ramp-up guide and customize as needed
Share the guide with new team members

tips.headline: Use the path parameter with EnterWorktree to switch between git worktrees
tips.summary: The EnterWorktree tool now accepts a path parameter that lets you switch into existing worktrees of your current repository. This makes it easier to work with multiple branches or feature development in parallel without switching repositories.
actionable_steps: Identify the worktree path you want to switch to in your current repository
Use the EnterWorktree tool with the path parameter: `EnterWorktree(path="/path/to/your/worktree")`
Verify you're in the correct worktree by checking the current branch or directory

tips.headline: Use ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H to extend prompt cache duration
tips.summary: Setting this environment variable enables 1-hour prompt cache TTL instead of the default, which can reduce API costs and improve response times for longer coding sessions. This works across API key, Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry deployments.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=true in your system or deployment configuration
Restart Claude Code to apply the new caching setting
Monitor your usage to verify extended caching is working

tips.headline: Use `/tui fullscreen` for flicker-free Claude Code rendering
tips.summary: The `/tui fullscreen` command switches Claude Code to a flicker-free rendering mode within the same conversation. This improves visual stability and reduces screen flicker during interactions.
actionable_steps: Open Claude Code
Type `/tui fullscreen` in the conversation
Press Enter to activate flicker-free rendering mode

tips.headline: Use `/terminal-setup` to configure smoother fullscreen scrolling in VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.116 improved terminal scrolling performance by automatically configuring your editor's scroll sensitivity. This eliminates choppy scrolling when working in fullscreen terminal mode.
actionable_steps: Open Claude Code in your VS Code, Cursor, or Windsurf editor
Run the `/terminal-setup` command
Allow Claude Code to configure your editor's scroll sensitivity settings

tips.headline: Enable forked subagents in external Claude Code builds
tips.summary: Forked subagents allow Claude Code to spawn separate agent processes for parallel task execution. This can improve performance for complex workflows that benefit from concurrent processing.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1
Restart Claude Code to apply the setting
Verify subagents are working by checking for multiple agent processes during complex tasks

tips.headline: Use visual mode in Claude Code for text selection and editing
tips.summary: Claude Code now supports vim-style visual mode (v) and visual-line mode (V) for selecting and manipulating text. This enables more efficient text editing workflows similar to vim editors.
actionable_steps: Press 'v' to enter visual mode for character-by-character selection
Press 'V' to enter visual-line mode for line-by-line selection
Use standard vim operators on your selected text

tips.headline: Configure persistent Claude Code settings using ~/.claude/settings.json
tips.summary: Claude Code now saves your /config preferences (theme, editor mode, verbose output) to a persistent file instead of resetting each session. This eliminates the need to reconfigure your preferences every time you start Claude Code.
actionable_steps: Run Claude Code and use /config to set your preferred theme, editor mode, and other settings
Verify settings are saved to ~/.claude/settings.json file
Test persistence by restarting Claude Code and confirming settings remain

tips.headline: Use `alwaysLoad: true` in MCP server config to skip tool-search deferral
tips.summary: By default, Claude Code defers loading some MCP tools until they're needed. Setting `alwaysLoad: true` in your MCP server configuration ensures all tools from that server are immediately available without waiting for tool search to activate them.
actionable_steps: Open your MCP server configuration file
Add `"alwaysLoad": true` to the server config object
Restart Claude Code to apply the changes

tips.headline: Use `claude plugin prune` to clean up orphaned plugin dependencies
tips.summary: Auto-installed plugin dependencies can accumulate over time, taking up disk space. The prune command removes dependencies that are no longer needed by any installed plugins.
actionable_steps: Run `claude plugin prune` in your terminal
Alternatively, use `claude plugin uninstall --prune [plugin-name]` to uninstall a plugin and clean up its dependencies in one step

tips.headline: Set ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER to control AWS Bedrock performance
tips.summary: You can now configure which AWS Bedrock service tier Claude Code uses by setting an environment variable. This lets you choose between default performance, flexible pricing, or priority processing depending on your needs.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER to one of: 'default', 'flex', or 'priority'
Restart Claude Code to apply the new service tier setting
Verify the tier is active by checking that requests include the X-Amzn-Bedrock-Service-Tier header

tips.headline: Use claude project purge to clean up Claude Code project state
tips.summary: The new purge command removes all Claude Code artifacts for a project including transcripts, tasks, file history, and config entries. This is useful for cleaning up projects or starting fresh without manual file deletion.
actionable_steps: Run 'claude project purge [path]' to delete all Claude Code state for a project
Use '--dry-run' flag first to preview what will be deleted
Add '-y' or '--yes' to skip confirmation prompts, or '-i' for interactive mode

tips.headline: Use bare /color command to randomize your Claude Code session color
tips.summary: The /color command without arguments now automatically selects a random color for your session. This provides a quick way to visually distinguish different sessions without manually choosing colors.
actionable_steps: Open Claude Code terminal
Type `/color` (without any arguments)
Press Enter to apply a random session color

tips.headline: Use CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN to keep conversation in terminal scrollback
tips.summary: Claude Code normally uses a fullscreen alternate-screen renderer that clears when you exit. Setting this environment variable keeps your conversation in your terminal's native scrollback buffer, making it easier to review past interactions after closing Claude Code.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable: export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1
Launch Claude Code as normal
Your conversation will now remain in terminal scrollback when you exit

tips.headline: Configure worktree base reference to preserve unpushed commits
tips.summary: The latest Claude Code update changed the default behavior for worktrees to branch from origin instead of local HEAD, potentially losing unpushed commits. Setting the baseRef to 'head' preserves your local work when creating new worktrees.
actionable_steps: Open your Claude Code settings
Add or modify the setting: "worktree.baseRef": "head"
Save the configuration file

tips.headline: Enable feedback surveys for enterprise OpenTelemetry users
tips.summary: If your enterprise captures telemetry data through OpenTelemetry, you can now re-enable Claude Code's session quality surveys to gather user feedback. This helps organizations collect structured feedback data alongside their existing telemetry infrastructure.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY_FOR_OTEL=true
Restart your Claude Code application
Verify that session quality surveys now appear in your Claude Code interface

tips.headline: Use case-insensitive agent type names in Claude Code configurations
tips.summary: Claude Code now accepts agent type names with any casing and separators. This makes configuration more flexible and reduces errors from formatting inconsistencies.
actionable_steps: In your Claude Code configuration, use any casing for agent types (e.g., 'Code Reviewer', 'code-reviewer', 'CODE_REVIEWER')
Test that your existing configurations still work with the new flexible matching
Update documentation to reflect the more flexible naming convention

tips.headline: Use terminalSequence field to enable desktop notifications from Claude Code hooks
tips.summary: The terminalSequence field allows Claude Code hooks to emit desktop notifications, window titles, and terminal bells even when running without a controlling terminal. This is particularly useful for background processes or automated workflows that need to communicate status updates to users.
actionable_steps: Update your hook JSON output to include the terminalSequence field
Configure the field to emit the desired notification type (desktop notification, window title, or bell)
Test the hook in an environment without a controlling terminal to verify notifications work

tips.headline: Use --add-dir flag to configure Claude agents with additional directories
tips.summary: The new --add-dir flag allows you to specify additional directories for Claude agents to access during background sessions. This expands the scope of files and resources your agent can work with beyond the default project directory.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.142 or later
Run 'claude agents --add-dir /path/to/additional/directory' when starting an agent session
Verify the agent can access files in the specified directory

tips.headline: Use `claude agents --json` to integrate Claude sessions with external tools
tips.summary: The new JSON output format allows you to programmatically access live Claude session information. This enables integration with terminal multiplexers like tmux, status bars, and custom session management tools.
actionable_steps: Run `claude agents --json` in your terminal to see the JSON output format
Parse the JSON output in your scripts to extract session information
Integrate the JSON data with tools like tmux-resurrect or custom status bars
Set up automated session monitoring or management based on the structured data

tips.headline: Use `/code-review` with effort levels for better code analysis
tips.summary: The `/simplify` command has been renamed to `/code-review` and now accepts optional effort levels like 'high' for more thorough analysis. This gives you better control over how deeply Claude examines your code for potential improvements.
actionable_steps: Replace any existing `/simplify` commands with `/code-review`
Add effort levels like `/code-review high` for more thorough analysis
Use `/code-review low` for quick reviews or `/code-review medium` for standard analysis

tips.headline: Pin Claude Code sessions to keep them alive during idle periods
tips.summary: Pinned sessions in Claude Code now persist even when not actively used and are only terminated under memory pressure after non-pinned sessions are closed first. This prevents losing your work context during breaks or when switching between tasks.
actionable_steps: Open Claude Code and start an agents session
Press Ctrl+T to pin the current session
The session will now remain active even during idle periods

tips.headline: Use /usage command to track Claude Code resource consumption by category
tips.summary: The /usage command now provides detailed breakdowns of what's consuming your usage limits, including skills, subagents, plugins, and MCP server costs. This helps identify which features are driving your resource consumption for better optimization.
actionable_steps: Type /usage in Claude Code
Review the per-category breakdown showing skills, subagents, plugins, and MCP-server costs
Identify high-usage categories to optimize your workflow

tips.headline: Use `/code-review --fix` to automatically apply review findings
tips.summary: Instead of manually implementing code review suggestions, this command automatically applies reuse, simplification, and efficiency improvements to your working tree. This streamlines the code review process by eliminating the manual step of implementing suggested changes.
actionable_steps: Run `/code-review --fix` command in Claude Code
Review the automatically applied changes in your working tree
Verify the improvements match your expectations

tips.headline: Use `/reload-skills` to refresh skills without restarting
tips.summary: When you add or modify Claude Code skills, you can reload them instantly without losing your current session context. This saves time during skill development and testing workflows.
actionable_steps: Make changes to your skill files
Run `/reload-skills` command in Claude Code
Verify new or updated skills are available in the current session

tips.headline: Configure `disallowed-tools` in skill frontmatter to restrict model access
tips.summary: You can prevent Claude from using specific tools while a skill is active by declaring them in the skill's frontmatter. This gives you fine-grained control over tool availability during skill execution.
actionable_steps: Open your skill file
Add `disallowed-tools: ["tool1", "tool2"]` to the frontmatter section
Save the file and reload skills with `/reload-skills`
Test that the specified tools are unavailable when the skill is active

tips.headline: Set up MCP servers to extend Claude's capabilities
tips.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers allow Claude to connect to external services like databases, APIs, and monitoring tools. This dramatically expands what Claude can do beyond just code editing.
actionable_steps: Create or locate a `.mcp.json` file in your project
Add server configuration with connection details
Install the MCP server using Claude Code's MCP management
Verify the connection and test available tools

tips.headline: Create a CLAUDE.md file to provide project context
tips.summary: CLAUDE.md files give Claude persistent knowledge about your project's structure, conventions, and requirements. This helps Claude make better decisions and follow your specific guidelines consistently.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md file in your project root
Add project overview, coding standards, and key architectural decisions
Include file structure explanations and important context
Test that Claude references this information in its responses

tips.headline: Use CLAUDE.md files to provide persistent context for your projects
tips.summary: CLAUDE.md files let you give Claude permanent instructions and context about your project that persist across conversations. Claude automatically loads these files when working in your codebase, eliminating the need to repeatedly explain project structure and conventions.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md file in your project root directory
Write clear instructions about your project's structure, conventions, and requirements
Add import statements for additional context files if needed

tips.headline: Set up hooks to automate Claude Code workflows at key events
tips.summary: Hooks allow you to run custom scripts or commands automatically when specific events occur in Claude Code, such as session start, prompt submission, or instruction loading. This enables automated setup, validation, or custom integrations.
actionable_steps: Create hook configuration files in your project's .claude directory
Define hook events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, etc.) and their corresponding actions
Configure hook handlers with command, HTTP, or MCP tool fields as needed
Test hooks using the /hooks menu to verify they trigger correctly

tips.headline: Organize project rules using .claude/rules/ directory structure
tips.summary: The .claude/rules/ directory lets you break down complex project instructions into organized, manageable files. This makes it easier to maintain large codebases and share specific rules across multiple projects.
actionable_steps: Create a .claude/rules/ directory in your project root
Split your CLAUDE.md instructions into focused rule files (e.g., coding-style.md, testing.md)
Use symlinks to share common rules across multiple projects
Reference rule files from your main CLAUDE.md using import statements

tips.headline: Use /effort xhigh command for complex tasks requiring maximum processing power
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.154 introduced the /effort xhigh command which enables high-effort processing mode for challenging tasks. This mode is now the default in Opus 4.8 and provides enhanced problem-solving capabilities for complex coding challenges.
actionable_steps: Type /effort xhigh at the beginning of your prompt or conversation
Present your most challenging coding task or problem
Allow Claude to process with maximum effort for better results

tips.headline: Enable acceptEdits mode for safer file modifications in Claude Code
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.160 introduced enhanced safety prompts in acceptEdits mode that warn before writing to potentially dangerous files like shell startup files and build configs. This prevents unintended command execution while still allowing necessary edits.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.160 or later
Enable acceptEdits mode in your Claude Code configuration
Review and approve prompts when Claude attempts to edit shell startup files or build configs
Test that the safety prompts appear when editing files like .zshenv, .npmrc, or .pre-commit-config.yaml

tips.headline: Set up OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES to track Claude Code usage by team
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.161 now includes OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES values as labels on metric datapoints. This allows you to slice and analyze usage metrics by custom dimensions like team, repository, or project. Essential for organizations wanting to track and optimize Claude usage across different groups.
actionable_steps: Set the OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES environment variable with your desired labels (e.g., 'team=backend,repo=api-service')
Restart Claude Code to apply the new resource attributes
Check your metrics dashboard to verify the new labels appear on datapoints
Create queries or dashboards filtering by your custom dimensions

tips.headline: Use /plugin list command to manage Claude Code plugins
tips.summary: The new /plugin list command helps you track which plugins are installed and their status. You can filter to see only enabled or disabled plugins, making plugin management much easier.
actionable_steps: Type `/plugin list` in Claude Code to see all installed plugins
Use `/plugin list --enabled` to see only active plugins
Use `/plugin list --disabled` to see only inactive plugins

tips.headline: Configure fallback models for better reliability when primary model fails
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.166 introduced a fallbackModel setting that lets you specify up to three backup models that will be tried in order when your primary model is overloaded or unavailable. This prevents workflow interruptions during high-traffic periods.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.166 or later
Add 'fallbackModel' setting to your configuration with up to 3 model names in priority order
Use '--fallback-model' flag when starting interactive sessions to apply fallbacks
Test the configuration by temporarily blocking access to your primary model

tips.headline: Use safe-mode flag to troubleshoot Claude Code issues
tips.summary: When Claude Code behaves unexpectedly, safe mode disables all customizations including CLAUDE.md files, plugins, skills, hooks, and MCP servers. This helps isolate whether issues stem from your configurations or the base application.
actionable_steps: Run `claude-code --safe-mode` from your terminal
Alternatively, set the environment variable `CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE=true`
Test if your issue persists in safe mode
If the issue disappears, gradually re-enable customizations to identify the culprit

tips.headline: Configure AWS region in ~/.aws config files for Bedrock integration
tips.summary: Claude Code now reads AWS region from your local AWS config files when AWS_REGION environment variable isn't set. This follows AWS SDK precedence rules and simplifies setup for Bedrock users.
actionable_steps: Create or edit ~/.aws/config file
Add [default] section with region = your-aws-region (e.g., us-east-1)
Remove or unset AWS_REGION environment variable to test the fallback
Use /status command in Claude Code to verify the region source

tips.headline: Set language setting to control session title generation
tips.summary: Claude Code now generates session titles in the language of your conversation. You can pin a specific language to ensure consistent title generation regardless of conversation content.
actionable_steps: Open Claude Code settings
Locate the 'language' setting
Set it to your preferred language code (e.g., 'en', 'es', 'fr')

tips.headline: Set an idle timeout for AskUserQuestion dialogs via /config
tips.summary: In Claude Code v2.1.200, AskUserQuestion dialogs no longer auto-continue by default. If you want dialogs to proceed automatically after inactivity, you now need to explicitly opt into an idle timeout.
actionable_steps: Run `/config` inside Claude Code
Locate the idle timeout setting for AskUserQuestion dialogs
Enable and set your desired timeout value

tips.headline: Update permission mode references to 'manual' after upgrading Claude Code
tips.summary: The default permission mode across CLI, VS Code, and JetBrains is now called 'Manual' instead of 'default'. Existing configs using 'default' still work, but scripts or docs referencing the old name should be updated for clarity.
actionable_steps: Search your configs and scripts for `--permission-mode default` or `"defaultMode": "default"`
Replace with `--permission-mode manual` or `"defaultMode": "manual"`
Verify behavior matches expectations in CLI, VS Code, and JetBrains integrations

tips.headline: Ensure disabledMcpServers/enabledMcpServers are arrays in .claude.json
tips.summary: A startup crash occurred when these fields were set to non-array values in .claude.json. Setting them correctly as arrays avoids this crash after upgrading Claude Code.
actionable_steps: Open your .claude.json file
Check the `disabledMcpServers` and `enabledMcpServers` fields
Ensure both are formatted as arrays (e.g., `[]` or `["server1"]`), not strings or objects

tips.headline: Podcast: The AI Daily Brief keeps you current in 20 minutes a day
tips.summary: The AI Daily Brief by Nathaniel Whittemore delivers daily news analysis on everything AI — from new model releases and agent tooling to the practical questions of how AI changes work. A good audio companion to this site: listen on the commute, then dig into the Claude-specific details here.
actionable_steps: Search for 'The AI Daily Brief' in your podcast app (Apple Podcasts, Spotify) or visit aidailybrief.ai
Episodes are ~20 minutes — fits a commute or coffee break
The headline segment covers the day's biggest story; stay for the analysis

sources.title: The AI Daily Brief — official site

tips.headline: Use the Dynamic Workflow Size setting to control agent counts
tips.summary: Claude Code v2.1.202 adds a 'Dynamic workflow size' option in /config that lets you guide how many agents Claude spawns for dynamic workflows (small/medium/large). This is an advisory setting, not a hard cap, so it helps balance speed vs. thoroughness for multi-agent tasks.
actionable_steps: Run /config in Claude Code
Locate the 'Dynamic workflow size' setting
Set it to small, medium, or large based on task complexity and desired agent count

tips.headline: Use workflow.run_id and workflow.name OTel attributes to trace workflow runs
tips.summary: Claude Code now emits workflow.run_id and workflow.name as OpenTelemetry attributes on telemetry from workflow-spawned agents. This lets teams reconstruct the full activity of a workflow run from their observability backend.
actionable_steps: Ensure OpenTelemetry export is configured for your Claude Code instance
Query your OTel backend for workflow.run_id and workflow.name attributes
Filter/group traces by these attributes to reconstruct a workflow run's activity
